title: Design peer review
idea: A design peer review is a short session where a colleague tests your class model against the requirements and against likely changes, and you record each decision.
points: Present in order: requirements, class diagram, one lifecycle, then the demo output.
Reviewers ask change questions: what must you edit to add a new channel?
Answer with the class that changes; if many classes change, note a design fix.
Swap roles afterwards; reviewing another design shows you what interviewers look for.

hero.title: What a reviewer checks
head: Area
Question to ask
Red flag
rows: No class or check traces to it
Who asks for changes to this class?
One service edited for every ticket
Which moves are illegal, and where is that enforced?
What edits does a new pricing rule need?
An if-else grows in the service
What does the caller see when a slot is taken?
Which output shows the failure path ran?
Only the happy path was run
hero.caption: Ask one row at a time. Write down each red flag found and the class that would fix it.

pitfalls: Defending every choice; log the feedback and decide later with the requirements in hand.
Reviewing style or naming first; check responsibilities and change cost before cosmetics.
takeaway: A good review asks what changes, and which class absorbs it.
